title: Ephemeral-quant warmstart with hot-right-sizing for sub-second OOM recovery
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: During peak multi-tenant workloads we observe transient OOMs caused by KV cache growth and bursty long-context requests. Current mitigation (eviction + fallback to smaller models) works but incurs high request latency and token loss for in-flight streams. We need a fast, low-latency recovery path that preserves in-flight context and minimizes user-visible degradation.

Proposal: Implement an "ephemeral-quant warmstart" flow combined with hot-right-sizing of batch admission windows and delta KV checkpointing. When an OOM sentinel triggers, the runtime will: (1) atomically create a compact, quantized ephemeral variant of the model in GPU memory using a precompiled quant profile (int8/int4 transcription) and a zero-copy mapping for weights that can be warmed in tens of ms; (2) shrink the current batch admission window (hot-right-sizing) to reduce peak working set while preserving prefix tokens; (3) stream a delta KV checkpoint to host-backed fast NVMe and mount a read-only micro-snapshot into the ephemeral model to restore prefix KV state without full re-materialization; (4) transparently route in-flight requests to the ephemeral quantized path with an adjusted sampling policy to preserve semantics; (5) if ephemeral path capacity is exceeded, ladder fallback to a cheaper hetero-model hosted on CPU for tail shards.

Key user goals: sub-second recovery, minimal token truncation, predictable p99 latency, and graceful fidelity degradation (not total request failure).
acceptance_criteria: When a controlled OOM is injected in staging, 90% of affected streaming requests recover on the ephemeral-quant path within 750ms without dropping prefix tokens.
P99 latency for recovered requests stays below 2x baseline and median below 1.3x baseline during recovery window.
No silent correctness regressions: automated evals on a representative prompt set show <=3% quality delta (ROUGE/BLEU/LLR) vs the primary model during recovery scenarios.
Operational: dashboards expose recovery count, mean recovery time, tokens-offloaded, and fallback-to-hetero-model rate; alerts when fallback rate >1% per minute.
Rollout gated by canary traffic (5% traffic) and manual approval after 48h of stable metrics in canary.
design_notes:
Trade-offs considered: full model swap is reliable but too slow; aggressive KV eviction reduces quality and induces more cache churn. Ephemeral quant lets us keep same compute graph and KV layout while reducing memory footprint. The main complexity is ensuring fast quant warmstart without kernel JIT stalls — we will rely on precompiled quant kernels for supported model families and maintain an LRU of pre-warmed quant footprints per GPU. Delta KV checkpointing stores only modified attention blocks since last checkpoint to minimize I/O. Hot-right-sizing adapts batch admission window per-GPU based on free memory headroom and ongoing request latencies. If ephemeral warmstart is unsupported (legacy model), fall back to the existing degrade-and-evict path.

Security/compat: ephemeral weights are stored encrypted at rest; KMS keys scoped to cluster and destroyed after the ephemeral exists. Audit logs record model warmstart and fallback events.
implementation_steps: Add precompile pipeline for int8/int4 ephemeral weight footprints and CI job to validate kernel correctness.
Implement ephemeral-quant allocator: zero-copy map + fast page population for weights using async memcpy and pinned host buffers.
Delta KV checkpoint format: protobuf schema + NVMe micro-snapshot writer/reader with versioning and checksums.
Hot-right-sizing admission controller: mem-headroom estimator + sliding window rule to shrink/expand batch admission.
Routing shim: per-request circuit to move to ephemeral variant and back; expose tracing to link original request and recovered stream.
End-to-end integration tests with OOM-injection harness and golden prompt suites; load test with canary traffic generator.
Dashboard and alerting: grafana panels, SLO burn-down, and PagerDuty playbook update.
rollout_plan: Canary on one Dedicated pool (eu-west-1) at 5% traffic for 48h. Step up to 25% after 72h if fallback rate <0.5% and p99 latency within target. Full rollout after manual sign-off and ops runbook update. Include kill-switch to revert to current eviction+fallback strategy instantly.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Asha: Spike complete for quant warmstart prototype. Warmstart time on p4d: median 120ms when weight footprint precompiled; cold compile is ~1.8s (unacceptable). Need precompile coverage for top-4 model families.
2025-02-18 - Liam: Implemented delta KV checkpoint writer. Initial writes are ~30KB per active conversation per minute in our synthetic workload. Need to cap retention and GC aggressively.
2025-02-22 - Maya Chen (PM): Prioritize canary pool in eu-west-1 due to predictable traffic and smaller variance. Please add dashboard panels for tokens-offloaded and per-request fidelity score.

2025-02-26 - Oliver Grant (SRE): Observed a JIT stall when ephemeral path triggered concurrently on >8 slots; mitigation: stagger warmstarts using backoff and maintain a small pre-warmed pool per GPU.
2025-03-04 - Liam: Integration tests passing locally. Next: run the OOM-injection harness in staging and validate acceptance criteria.
